articles.title: Agile Robots raises $500 million led by SoftBank
articles.snippet: Agile Robots raises $500 million led by SoftBank CASRAI
articles.text:
Munich-based Agile Robots announced on November 12, 2026 that it had closed a $500 million Series F led by SoftBank Group, with NVIDIA among the participants. The financing supports international expansion and manufacturing, putting fresh capital behind a robotics business whose research connections include Franka Robotics and a Google DeepMind partnership. Reuters confirmed the announcement .
A $500 million round for expansion and production
The round values Agile Robots at $8.5 billion and takes its total funding to $2 billion. Alongside SoftBank and NVIDIA, participants include Hitachi Group, comprising Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures, and T.Capital. The company’s November 12 announcement says the proceeds will support a larger presence in the United States, additional production capacity including in Germany, and entry into new markets.
Founder and chief executive Zhaopeng Chen described the financing as a way to accelerate expansion and bring intelligent robots into industrial production. SoftBank Investment Advisers managing partner Dennis Chang said Agile combines robotics expertise with industrial execution, adding: “We believe Physical AI will transform industries.” These are the company’s and investor’s expectations for the business.
Tech.eu’s November 12 report places the investment in an existing industrial operation: Agile’s machines assemble products, handle components, inspect equipment and move materials through factories. Its portfolio extends across robotic arms, hands, autonomous mobile robots and humanoids, together with their software and AI models.
Factory capacity and installed systems measure different things
Reuters reported that Agile opened its Fürstenfeldbruck factory, near Munich, earlier in 2026. The company says it can produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually. That is a stated capacity ceiling, rather than a report of annual output or shipments.
Separately, Agile reports more than 20,000 robotic solutions installed worldwide. Its announcement describes deployments across automotive, consumer electronics, logistics and other industries; it does not identify that total as humanoid installations. Treating the two numbers as interchangeable would obscure the difference between the company’s established industrial business and its humanoid manufacturing ambitions.
The financing release also gives no allocation of the proceeds between the United States, German production and other markets. It therefore establishes the expansion priorities without quantifying how much additional capacity each location will receive.
A research spin-off with an academic hardware connection
Agile was founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center, according to Reuters and Tech.eu. The company reports more than 2,000 research and development specialists and over 650 patents. Its path from a public research institution into industrial automation provides a concrete technology transfer connection for universities following the investment.
There is also a direct research equipment link. Franka Robotics says it has belonged to Agile Robots since 2023. Franka describes its Research 3 system as a force-sensitive platform for robotics and AI, giving researchers low-level access to robot control and learning capabilities. Its website also says Agile’s Diana 7 now supports the Franka Control Interface, extending the ecosystem to a robot with greater reach and payload capacity.

VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:35 PM
VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
VICI Properties, a real estate investment trust specializing in gaming, hospitality, entertainment, and experiential properties, has secured a new $500 million unsecured term loan through its subsidiary VICI Properties L.P. The financing will be used to partially refinance the company’s outstanding senior unsecured notes maturing in February 2027, while an accompanying amendment reduces borrowing costs under its existing $2.5 billion revolving credit facility.
The new loan matures on January 31, 2032, extending a portion of VICI’s debt maturity profile by approximately five years.
The loan initially carries an interest rate of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 90 basis points, based on a pricing grid tied to the subsidiary’s credit ratings.
The agreement also includes an improvement in pricing when the company’s total leverage ratio is at or below a specified threshold.
VICI drew the entire $500 million at closing and entered into swap agreements covering the full principal amount.
These arrangements establish an effective all-in fixed interest rate of approximately 5.20%.
The financing will help VICI address a meaningful portion of its February 2027 debt maturity by partially redeeming and refinancing its 5.75% senior unsecured notes.
By replacing part of the approaching maturity with longer-dated financing, VICI is seeking to improve its debt maturity schedule and maintain financial flexibility.
The transaction also diversifies the company’s available funding sources.
Alongside the term loan, VICI amended its existing $2.5 billion unsecured revolving credit facility.
The amendment lowers the applicable interest rate from SOFR plus 85 basis points to SOFR plus 80 basis points, subject to the company’s ratings-based pricing grid and leverage-related adjustments.
The revolving facility’s borrowing capacity and maturity remain unchanged.
These changes provide VICI with improved pricing on a significant source of corporate liquidity.
Wells Fargo Securities served as sole bookrunner for the term loan, while Wells Fargo Bank acted as administrative agent.
Wells Fargo Securities, Mizuho Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, and Truist Securities served as joint lead arrangers.
Additional participating financial institutions included Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Capital One, Citizens Bank, Scotiabank, Barclays, Citibank, Goldman Sachs Bank USA, and Texas Capital Bank.
VICI Properties maintains one of the largest portfolios of experiential real estate assets in North America.
The company’s holdings include 103 experiential properties, comprising 63 gaming properties and 40 other experiential assets across the United States and Canada.
Its portfolio encompasses approximately 130 million square feet and includes more than 67,000 hotel rooms and over 700 restaurants, bars, nightclubs, and sportsbooks.
Major holdings include Caesars Palace Las Vegas, MGM Grand, and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas.
The company leases its properties to gaming, hospitality, and entertainment operators under long-term triple-net lease agreements.

VulcanForms: $500 Million Financing Led By J.P. Morgan And Apollo To Build Three New U.S. Manufacturing Factories
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 14, 2026
VulcanForms: $500 Million Financing Led By J.P. Morgan And Apollo To Build Three New U.S. Manufacturing Factories
VulcanForms, a Boston-based advanced digital manufacturing company, has secured an agreement for $500 million in financing led by J.P. Morgan and funds managed by Apollo. The financing will support construction of three new factories, expansion of domestic production capacity, and further development of the company’s integrated manufacturing platform as it responds to demand from customers across aerospace, defense, medical devices, consumer products, and industrial markets.
The transaction will help VulcanForms expand beyond its three existing manufacturing sites, bringing its planned manufacturing footprint to six facilities.
The company has secured multibillion-dollar commercial programs spanning several industries that require complex, high-performance metal components.
VulcanForms combines metal additive manufacturing, precision machining, automation, and physical AI within a unified production system designed to manufacture engineered parts at industrial scale.
The new financing is part of JPMorganChase’s Security and Resiliency Initiative, which supports investment in industries and supply chains considered important to U.S. economic security.
Building Three Additional Advanced Manufacturing Facilities
VulcanForms plans to use the financing to accelerate construction of three factories that will expand its domestic manufacturing capabilities.
The company currently operates manufacturing facilities in Devens and Newburyport, Massachusetts.
Its expansion reflects growing demand for advanced manufacturing services among customers seeking domestic production of sophisticated metal components.
These products frequently require specialized production processes, high manufacturing tolerances, and extensive quality validation.
Traditional manufacturing approaches can involve multiple suppliers responsible for different stages of production.
VulcanForms is developing an integrated alternative that combines several manufacturing processes within a coordinated digital infrastructure.
The company believes this approach can reduce production complexity, improve efficiency, and help manufacturers respond more quickly to changing customer requirements.
The additional facilities will provide capacity to support existing commercial programs and future production opportunities.
Combining Metal Additive Manufacturing And Physical AI
VulcanForms’ manufacturing platform integrates metal additive manufacturing with precision machining, automation, and AI-driven production capabilities.
Metal additive manufacturing uses digital designs to produce components through a process that builds material into a desired shape.
This approach can enable complex geometries that may be difficult to manufacture through conventional methods.
However, industrial production often requires additional processing to achieve precise dimensions, surface finishes, and performance characteristics.
VulcanForms addresses these requirements by combining additive manufacturing with precision machining and product validation.
The company also incorporates physical AI into its manufacturing infrastructure.

articles.text:
Renewables
Exus Renewables North America Closes $345 Million in Financing to Support New Projects
Press Release
Monday, November 16, 2026
SHARE:
Exus Renewables North America, an independent owner, developer, and operator of utility-scale renewable energy and energy storage projects, has announced the closing of $345 million in senior secured holding company financing led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The financing will support construction costs and the development of new projects across Exus’ growing U.S. portfolio of wind, solar and battery storage assets.
The financing announced November 12 builds on an active year for Exus , including the closing of a $400 million senior secured corporate credit facility in December and approximately $356 million in project-level construction financing for its Highland North and Cambria wind projects in Pennsylvania in July . With more than 800 MW operating or under construction and a total portfolio exceeding 6 GW, Exus continues to advance its project pipeline amid rising U.S. electricity demand.
“We have projects moving forward and a deep pipeline behind them, and this financing lets us keep that momentum going,” said Jim Spencer, president and CEO of Exus Renewables North America. “The support from Goldman Sachs Alternatives reflects confidence in our team and our projects, and gives us the flexibility to keep building and bring new generation online where it’s needed.”
“Exus has established a strong platform for developing and operating utility-scale renewable energy projects,” said Vikas Agrawal, managing director and co-head of Energy Transition Climate Credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. “We’re pleased to support its continued investment in new energy infrastructure as electricity demand grows across the United States.”
PEI Global Partners served as financial advisor to Exus on the transaction. Latham & Watkins LLP served as legal counsel to Exus, while Vinson & Elkins LLP served as legal counsel to Goldman Sachs Alternatives.
—This content was contributed by the communications team for Exus Renewables North America .

Salesforce stock: Salesforce Ventures leads US$290 million Q-CTRL round
Published on 11/16/2026 at 17:11 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS
Salesforce stock is in focus after Salesforce Ventures led Q-CTRL's US$290 million round. The November 12 financing targets quantum software and GPS-free navigation.
Q-CTRL round broadens Salesforce's AI reach
Salesforce Ventures led an oversubscribed US$290 million Series C round for Q-CTRL on November 12.
Q-CTRL plans to scale its quantum software and navigation business globally across finance, energy, autonomy and aerospace.
Salesforce, US79466L3024, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Salesforce Ventures led a US$290 million Series C funding round for quantum infrastructure software company Q-CTRL on November 12. The oversubscribed financing gives Salesforce's venture operation a prominent role in a private quantum technology investment and adds a new strategic angle ahead of Salesforce's next results.
Q-CTRL announced the financing in its Q-CTRL announcement . The company said the round reached US$290 million, equivalent to A$415 million, after two expansions to meet investor demand. Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners made significant contributions, while other new and returning investors included AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, In-Q-Tel and Lockheed Martin Ventures.
Quantum software becomes the focus
Q-CTRL said it will use the new capital to strengthen its software-first strategy and expand globally. Its products target quantum computing and sensing, including Ironstone Opal, a navigation system designed for use when GPS is unavailable or denied.
Robert Keith, a Salesforce Ventures partner, said Q-CTRL's AI-powered control software addresses the challenge of turning quantum hardware output into useful results. For Salesforce, the investment broadens exposure to a technology layer that could support enterprise computing, autonomy and aerospace applications, although Q-CTRL remains a private company outside Salesforce's core operating segments.

Q-CTRL: $290 Million Series C Funding Led By Salesforce Ventures Creates New Quantum Technology Unicorn
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 14, 2026
Q-CTRL: $290 Million Series C Funding Led By Salesforce Ventures Creates New Quantum Technology Unicorn
Q-CTRL, a developer of AI-powered quantum infrastructure software, has raised $290 million (A$415 million) in Series C funding led by Salesforce Ventures, with significant participation from Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners. The oversubscribed financing establishes Q-CTRL as a new quantum technology unicorn and provides capital to accelerate the commercialization of its quantum computing and sensing technologies across data centers, aviation, autonomous systems, and other industries.
The Series C round was expanded twice to accommodate investor demand and represents what the company describes as the largest fundraising round for a software-focused business in the quantum sector.
The investment will support Q-CTRL’s global expansion, continued development of its AI-powered quantum infrastructure platform, and commercialization of technologies designed to make quantum systems more reliable in real-world environments.
New investors include Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners, Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation, and SPARX Asset Management.
Returning investors include Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures, and Square Peg.
The investor group brings together venture capital firms, strategic corporate investors, and institutions with experience across AI, aerospace, defense, semiconductors, and industrial technologies.
Combining Artificial Intelligence And Quantum Computing
Q-CTRL develops infrastructure software designed to improve the performance and reliability of quantum technologies.
Its platform uses AI-powered control techniques to address technical challenges that have historically limited the practical application of quantum computing and quantum sensing.
Quantum systems are highly sensitive to environmental interference, noise, and other sources of error.
These challenges can reduce the accuracy and reliability of quantum operations, making it difficult to achieve useful results outside carefully controlled laboratory environments.
Q-CTRL’s software is designed to mitigate these limitations through techniques that improve how quantum hardware operates.
The company takes a hardware-agnostic approach, allowing its technologies to work across different quantum computing and sensing platforms.
According to Q-CTRL, its software can increase the effective computational capabilities of quantum machines by thousands of times in certain applications.
The company’s strategy focuses on making existing and emerging quantum hardware more useful rather than developing competing quantum processors.
This approach positions Q-CTRL as a provider of infrastructure software that could support multiple participants across the quantum technology industry.

Salesforce Ventures led the financing based on Q-CTRL’s progress in turning quantum technology into practical commercial applications.

articles.text:
ACWA Power , SA15CGS10H12
ACWA Power stock: $226 million financing closes for Uzbek wind farm
Published on 11/16/2026 at 00:08 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS
ACWA Power secured long-term financing for a wind project in Uzbekistan. The milestone supports the developer's international renewable-energy expansion.
Uzbekistan project reaches financing milestone
ACWA Power secured long-term funding for the Bash II wind farm in Uzbekistan.
The project strengthens the company’s development portfolio across energy and water infrastructure.
ACWA Power is expanding projects from its Riyadh headquarters across international markets.
ACWA Power, SA15CGS10H12, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
ACWA Power has reached financial close on the Bash II wind farm in Uzbekistan's Bukhara Region, according to Oil & Gas News on Sunday, November 15. The Saudi developer secured long-term financing of 226 million US dollars, equivalent to 847.5 million Saudi riyals, from a consortium of international lenders.
Financing advances Uzbekistan project
Bash II has a planned capacity of 300 megawatts and is located in Uzbekistan's Bukhara Region. Financial close marks the transition from project development toward construction and operation, although the report did not provide a commercial start date or identify the lending consortium.
For investors, the financing milestone adds to ACWA Power's pipeline of contracted and developing energy assets. The project also underlines the role of project finance in funding large renewable-energy installations without relying solely on corporate balance-sheet capital.
International energy and water platform
ACWA Power leads energy, water and green hydrogen projects from its headquarters in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Its activities span power generation, water desalination, renewable energy and storage projects across international markets. The company works with partners, customers and communities across multiple regions, giving its portfolio exposure to infrastructure demand beyond its home market.
